name: bundle_width
expr: cable_large_count * cable_large_diameter + cable_second_count * cable_second_diameter + flat_cable_width + (cable_items + 1) * cable_side_gap + if(separator_needed, separator_thickness + cable_side_gap, 0 mm)

name: second_count_max
expr: max(0, floor((bundle_width_limit - 2 * cable_side_gap - separator_thickness - cable_large_count * (cable_large_diameter + cable_side_gap)) / (cable_second_diameter + cable_side_gap)))

name: flat_width_max
expr: max(0 mm, bundle_width_limit - (cable_large_count * cable_large_diameter + cable_second_count * cable_second_diameter + (cable_large_count + cable_second_count + 2) * cable_side_gap + if(separator_needed, separator_thickness + cable_side_gap, 0 mm)))

name: wall_thickness
expr: clamp(ceil((0.16 * inner_height + 0.8 mm) / 0.1 mm) * 0.1 mm, 1.8 mm, 3.2 mm)

name: bar_thickness
expr: clamp(ceil((0.15 * inner_height + 0.8 mm + 0.012 * inner_width) / 0.1 mm) * 0.1 mm, 2 mm, 4 mm)

name: worst_flank_end
expr: (cheek_tip_length + stop_gap) / cos(30 deg) + half_height * tan(30 deg) + 1.4 mm

name: pitch_target
expr: max(2 * link_height, worst_flank_end + web_length + 0.6 * wall_thickness + snap_span_needed, 2 * cable_centre_radius_needed * stop_play)

name: flank_relief
expr: max(0.2 mm, (cheek_tip_length + 0.05 mm - rear_lower_x * cos(turn_angle)) / sin(turn_angle))

name: cable_section
expr: pi / 4 * (cable_large_count * cable_large_diameter^2 + cable_second_count * cable_second_diameter^2) + flat_cable_width * flat_cable_thickness

name: chain_section_estimate
expr: 4 * wall_thickness * link_height * 0.85 + 2 * web_length * inner_width * bar_thickness / pitch

name: travel_limit
expr: clamp(floor(2 * (free_span - pitch) / 5 mm) * 5 mm, 100 mm, 2000 mm)

name: bend_centre_x
expr: pivot_x - pitch / 2 * cos(roll_angle) + bend_radius * cos(turn_angle / 2) * sin(roll_angle)

name: bend_centre_z
expr: lower_hinge_z + pitch / 2 * sin(roll_angle) + bend_radius * cos(turn_angle / 2) * cos(roll_angle)

name: lid_snap_depth
expr: clamp(0.95 * 0.67 * lid_strain_limit * (arm_reach - 0.7 mm)^2 / arm_thickness, 0.2 mm, 0.55 mm)

name: lid_chamfer_length
expr: 2 * arm_inner_y - 2 * lid_root_radius + pi * lid_root_radius + 2 * (arm_root_z - lid_root_radius - barb_top_z)

cable_large_diameter
label: Largest cable: diameter
description: Outside diameter of the thickest cable or hose. It sets the inner height of the links (igus: largest diameter plus at least 10 %, at least 2 mm).

name: cable_large_count
label: Largest cable: how many
description: How many cables of that diameter lie side by side.

name: cable_second_diameter
label: Second cable: diameter
description: A second, thinner cable. If the two diameters together are no more than 1.2 times the inner height, a separator rib is added to every link, because igus says such cables must not lie loose on each other.

name: cable_second_count
label: Second cable: how many
description: How many of the thinner cable; 0 for none.

name: flat_cable_width
label: Flat ribbon cable: width
description: Width of a flat ribbon cable laid in the chain (it is taken to be no thicker than the largest round cable); 0 for none.

name: cable_bend_radius
label: Smallest bend your cable allows
description: From the cable's data sheet: its minimum bending radius for continuous flexing (when in doubt, 10 x diameter, the NFPA 79 rule igus quotes). The chain's bend is kept outside this for the thickest cable lying at the inside of the bend.

name: machine_travel
label: Travel of the machine
description: How far the moving end travels, from end to end. The chain length follows from it by igus' rule: half the travel plus the bend. The form stops at the longest travel whose upper run carries itself; beyond that it would need a guide trough, which this Jig does not design.

name: moving_end_height
label: Height of the moving end
description: Height of the moving end's mounting face above the fixed end's mounting face. It sets the bend radius; too low a value would bend your cable too tightly, so the form stops at the smallest height that fits the cable.

name: filament
label: Filament
description: What you print with. It sets how much the snap may be sprung and how hard the snap is to press home.

name: hinge_clearance
label: Hinge clearance for your printer
description: The running gap at the hinge, between tongue and cheek and in the pin hole. Tune for your printer: 0.3 mm for a well-tuned one, more if the links bind, less if they rattle.

name: carriage_position
label: Run the machine (%)
description: Where the moving end is along its travel: drag it and the chain rolls, the bend walking along at half the speed of the carriage.

name: show
label: Show
description: The chain on the machine with the drive, or the parts laid on the bed in print orientation: one link, one lid and the two end pieces (export this view as a 3MF; the form tells how many of each to print).

title: Cable drag chain
description: A printable cable drag chain for a CNC machine or 3D printer, designed from your cables and your machine: give the cable bundle, the machine's travel, the height of the moving end and the smallest bend your cable allows, and the Jig derives the link size, the pitch, the number of links and where the fixed end goes, by igus' published chain-length rule and filling rules. Links snap together on a 45-degree cone pin, with printed stops that set the bend and hold the runs straight, a snap-on lid and printed end pieces. Run it with the slider. To print, set Show to Print set and export as 3MF, choosing the four bodies Print link, Print lid, Print fixed end and Print moving end: they are already in print orientation; the form tells how many links and lids to print.
